key_insight: A generalized mixing-plane can conservatively couple compressor–combustor–turbine interfaces by solving a thermodynamically consistent mixed-out state for reacting, non-perfect-gas mixtures.
engineering_relevance: This enables steady whole-engine turbomachinery simulations with combustion products, improving the realism of multiphysics gas-turbine design and analysis.
method: Outer pressure-root search enforces the mixed-out pressure state.
Inner enthalpy inversion closes the reacting-mixture thermodynamics.
Physical checks and power-law pressure sampling improve robustness near low normal velocity.
evidence_signal: The method was validated on a quasi-1D interface test, a Darmstadt transonic compressor case, and a KJ66 micro-turbojet whole-engine simulation, with maximum relative mass-flow error below 0.11% and good agreement with experiments.
watch_item: The nested thermodynamic solve may be numerically stiff near the upper physical pressure bound, so robust initialization and bounds handling are important.
paper_title: Generalised Mixing-Plane Method for Compressible Reacting-Mixture Flows in Steady Multiphysics Turbomachinery Simulations
